about: The token <held-out> in a slot value becomes the absolute path of the held-out folder the runner copies beside the scratch project (never into it). Under protocol version 2 no task file names that folder: the task folder is the same in every arm, and arm D is told nothing of the suite. Here the `checklist` slot names it, beside the checklist file, exactly where the template hands its checklist to the critic; the same slot value reaches the builder as a declared input, and says the suite is not the builder's to read or run. The task text goes to every arm as written.
name: Parse page ranges

values.task: Add `parseRanges(text, pageCount)` in a new file, src/parse-ranges.mjs: it reads what a person typed into the print dialog's page box, such as "1-3,5" or "7", and returns the page numbers to print as an array. Pages are numbered from 1 to `pageCount`; parts are separated by commas, and a part is one page or a range written first-last. A `text` that is not a string, or a `pageCount` that is not a positive integer, throws a TypeError; a text that cannot be read as pages of this document throws a RangeError. Tests go in tests/parse-ranges.test.mjs.
values.checklist: docs/REVIEW-CHECKLIST.md and every case of the held-out suite <held-out>/parse-ranges-cases.test.mjs (the suite is outside this project and settles what the task leaves open; the critic runs it from the project root with `node --test <held-out>/parse-ranges-cases.test.mjs` and, for each case that fails, quotes the input and the expected result in REVIEW.md; it is the critic's alone, and the builder does not read or run it)
